# Walmart DataVentures UI Shared Components

[![Built with Looper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20With-Looper-blue.svg)](https://ci.falcon.walmart.com/job/luminate-shared-components/)
[![Build Status](https://ci.walmart.com/buildStatus/icon?job=global-governance/ui-gg-common-components)](https://ci.falcon.walmart.com/job/luminate-shared-components/)

Shared Components for the Walmart DataVentures will hold :

- All shareable components among all the UI modules as needed under Walmart DataVentures and its applications

### Required Extensions :

- ESLint (`dbaeumer.vscode-eslint`)
- Prettier (`esbenp.prettier-vscode`)
- Make sure Prettier is selected as the Default Formatter and "Format on save" is enabled.
- ESLint auto-fix is enabled on save

### Get Started

Install dependencies (npm is the recommended package manager)

```
npm i
```

Run storybook on localhost (http://localhost:6006)

```
npm start
```

Run tests with coverage

```
npm run test
```

Build a distributable package

```
npm run build
```

### Self-Review Before Peer Review

Before requesting peer review on your PR, run the **self-pr-review** command using Wibey (the AI coding assistant in VS Code). This performs an automated, multi-persona code review on your PR diff and catches common issues before your teammates ever look at the code.

#### Why use it?

- **Catches real bugs** — logic errors, null access, missing error handling, broken cross-file contracts
- **Validates test quality** — flags weak assertions, missing edge cases, and tests that would pass even if the feature were broken
- **Checks accessibility & performance** — missing ARIA attributes, unnecessary re-renders, large bundle imports
- **Finds security gaps** — XSS vectors, unsanitized input, type safety holes (`any` usage, incorrect narrowing)
- **Saves reviewer time** — your PR arrives cleaner, so peer review can focus on design and architecture instead of surface-level issues

#### How to run it

1. Push your branch and create a **Draft PR** on GitHub
2. Make sure you're checked out on that PR branch locally
3. Open **Wibey** — either the VS Code Extension (chat panel) or the Wibey CLI. If using the CLI, run `/custom` first before running `/self-pr-review`
4. Run:
   ```
   /self-pr-review
   ```
5. Wibey will analyze your diff, present a numbered list of findings, and ask which ones to auto-fix
6. After fixes are applied, it runs the formatter, linter, type checker, and tests automatically
7. If your working directory was clean, it commits the fixes for you
8. Push the changes, then mark your Draft PR as **Ready for Review**

#### What it reviews

The command runs **5 specialized reviewer personas** in parallel on your diff:

| Persona | Focus |
|---------|-------|
| **Bug Hunter** | Logic errors, null/undefined, race conditions, async gaps |
| **Test Skeptic** | Weak assertions, missing edge cases, meaningless tests |
| **Future Maintainer** | Readability, confusing names, inconsistent patterns |
| **Security Auditor** | XSS, type safety, secrets in code, input sanitization |
| **Perf & UX Guardian** | Re-renders, bundle size, accessibility, loading states |

Findings are deduplicated, cross-validated, and classified as **[Fix]** (must address) or **[Optional]** (nice-to-have). You choose which to apply.

#### What it produces

A review report is saved to your project root (e.g., `.self-review-pr-142.md`). The report includes all findings, the fixes applied, remaining items as checkboxes, and a complexity map of your changes.

#### Recommended workflow

```
git checkout -b feature/my-feature
# ... make your changes, commit, push ...
# Open a Draft PR on GitHub
/self-pr-review               ← run in Wibey VS Code Extension
# or in Wibey CLI: /custom then /self-pr-review
git push                      ← push the fixes
# Mark Draft PR as Ready for Review on GitHub
```

### Testing Setup (v7.10.4+)

Components use ResizeObserver for responsive behavior. Add this one-liner to your Jest setup:

```javascript
// jest.setup.js or setupTests.js
import { setupSharedComponentsTests } from '@walmart-dataventures/shared-components/testing';
setupSharedComponentsTests();
```

#### Basic Testing

Most tests work automatically with default dimensions (200x150):

```javascript
test('menu renders', () => {
  render(<MenuAction />);
  // ResizeObserver fires automatically with defaults
  expect(screen.getByRole('menu')).toBeInTheDocument();
});
```

#### Testing Responsive Behavior

Use `triggerResize()` to test how components respond to different sizes:

```javascript
import { triggerResize } from '@walmart-dataventures/shared-components/testing';

test('menu repositions when content is tall', () => {
  render(<MenuAction isOpen />);
  const menu = screen.getByRole('menu');

  // Simulate tall menu (should flip upward)
  triggerResize(menu, { width: 200, height: 800 });

  expect(menu).toHaveStyle({ transform: 'translateY(-750px)' });
});

test('accordion expands to show content', () => {
  render(<Accordion><AccordionItem>Content</AccordionItem></Accordion>);
  const panel = screen.getByRole('region');

  // Simulate content height
  triggerResize(panel, { width: 400, height: 250 });

  expect(panel).toHaveStyle({ maxHeight: '250px' });
});
```

#### Components Using ResizeObserver

These components may benefit from `triggerResize()` in tests:
- **MenuAction** - Dynamic dropdown positioning based on available space
- **Accordion** - Content height calculation for animations
- **InfoUnderline** - Overflow detection for tooltip display
- **Legend** - Text truncation detection
- **DvTable TagCell** - Responsive tag display and overflow handling

#### Upgrading from v7.10.x

Replace any manual ResizeObserver mocks:

```javascript
// ❌ Remove this:
global.ResizeObserver = class ResizeObserver {
  observe() {}
  disconnect() {}
  unobserve() {}
};

// ✅ Add this:
import { setupSharedComponentsTests } from '@walmart-dataventures/shared-components/testing';
setupSharedComponentsTests();
```

#### Troubleshooting

**Tests fail with "ResizeObserver is not defined"**
- Make sure you called `setupSharedComponentsTests()` in your Jest setup file
- Verify `setupFilesAfterEnv` is configured in `jest.config.js`

**Component doesn't respond to resize in tests**
- Use `triggerResize(element, { width, height })` to explicitly simulate resize
- Ensure you're triggering resize on the correct element (the one being observed)

**Type errors with triggerResize**
- Install type definitions: `npm i -D @types/jest`
- Import the helper: `import { triggerResize } from '@walmart-dataventures/shared-components/testing'`
